title: Pistachio and Sesame Dukkah
summary: Toasted pistachios and sesame with coriander, cumin and fennel seeds, black pepper and salt, crushed to a crunchy, fragrant sprinkle.
equipment: spice grinder or mortar and pestle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast the pistachios
steps.text: Warm the dry pan over medium heat, add the pistachios and stir for 3-4 min until they smell toasty and pick up a few golden spots. Spread them on a plate to cool completely so they chop cleanly.

steps.title: Toast the sesame
steps.text: Add the sesame seeds to the same pan and stir for 2-3 min until evenly golden. Move them to a separate plate straight away, as they scorch quickly.

steps.title: Grind the spices
steps.text: Toast the coriander, cumin and fennel seeds for 1-2 min until fragrant, let them cool for a minute, then grind finely with the pepper and salt.

steps.title: Crush and combine
steps.text: Pulse the cooled pistachios a few times, or chop them by hand, until they look like coarse gravel with no whole nuts left. Mix with the sesame seeds and ground spices.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Set the dukkah out with crusty bread and a small bowl of olive oil for dipping, or scatter it over salads, fried eggs, hummus and roast vegetables.

tips: Let the nuts cool fully before processing; warm nuts release oil and turn pasty.
Pulse in short bursts and stop early; the texture should stay crunchy.
Swap half the pistachios for blanched hazelnuts for a richer, earthier blend.
Toast each ingredient separately, as they brown at different speeds.
storage: Keep in an airtight jar at room temperature, away from heat and light, for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
